questions.q: What was Captain trained to be when he was young?
choices: An army horse
A racehorse
A plow horse
A circus horse
questions.evidence: Captain had been broken in and trained for an army horse

questions.q: Which war did Captain's first owner go to?
choices: The Crimean war
The war in America
A war in India
A war in France
questions.evidence: going out to the Crimean war

questions.q: What part of army life did Captain say was dreadful?
choices: Being sent over the sea in a great ship
Learning to turn with the other horses
Hearing the trumpet sound
Being groomed every morning
questions.evidence: when it came to being sent abroad over the sea in a great ship, he almost changed his mind

questions.q: How were the horses put onto the ship?
choices: They were lifted with strong straps and swung through the air
They walked up a wooden ramp
They swam out to the ship
They were led across a bridge
questions.evidence: they were obliged to put strong straps under our bodies

questions.q: Why did Captain say the horses were not afraid in battle?
choices: They felt their rider firm in the saddle and his hand steady
They could not hear the guns
They wore blinkers over their eyes
They had never seen a cannon before
questions.evidence: so long as we felt our rider firm in the saddle, and his hand steady on the bridle

questions.q: How did Captain feel about his first master?
choices: He trusted and loved him completely
He was afraid of him
He thought he was too strict
He hardly knew him
questions.evidence: I had such perfect trust in him

questions.q: What name did Captain's master call him on the morning of the battle?
choices: Bayard
Jack
Ginger
Duke
questions.evidence: We shall have a day of it to-day, Bayard, my beauty

questions.q: The master stroked Captain's neck more than ever before, "as if he were thinking of something else." What does this suggest?
choices: He sensed the day would be very dangerous
He was bored and wanted to go home
He was planning to sell Captain
He was trying to fix a sore on Captain's neck
questions.evidence: He stroked my neck that morning more, I think, than he had ever done before

questions.q: What happened to Captain right after his master was struck and fell?
choices: The rush of the charge drove him away from the spot
He stood guard over his master all day
He galloped straight back to the stables
He was shot and fell beside his master
questions.evidence: by the force of their charge I was driven from the spot

questions.q: After Captain was left alone on the battlefield, what happened next?
choices: A soldier whose horse had been killed mounted him
His master got up and rode him again
He ran away into the woods
A farrier took him back to camp
questions.evidence: a soldier whose horse had been killed under him caught at my bridle and mounted me

questions.q: "Our gallant company was cruelly overpowered." What does "overpowered" mean here?
choices: Beaten by a stronger force
Given extra strength
Made very tired from waiting
Sent home early
questions.evidence: our gallant company was cruelly overpowered

questions.q: About how many horses from Captain's stables came back from that battle?
choices: About one in four
Almost all of them
About half
None except Captain
questions.evidence: In our stables there was only about one in four that returned

questions.q: What is the main lesson Captain teaches Black Beauty about war?
choices: War may look fine on parade, but it is terrible when men and horses are killed
War is the best way for a horse to become famous
Army horses have the easiest life of all horses
Horses understand why wars are fought
questions.evidence: when thousands of good brave men and horses are killed or crippled for life, it has a very different look
